correctness.rationale: The blowup Picard basis and Bezout inequalities prove there are exactly eleven negative curves (nine (-1), two (-2)). Adjunction and -K nefness rule out unlisted negative curves. A Schur-complement characterization proves an iff for all negative-definite supports. The stable-support descent follows because a Galois-stable sum of selected curves and a rational ample divisor furnish a rational big class in the chamber. The exact-matrix and independent incidence verifiers agree on all 2048 subsets, the five fixed profiles (221,61,17,23,5), root counts, identical cycle lengths for the two involutions, and 52 D8 orbits. A direct orbit computation and Burnside sum agree; explicit finite-field configurations realize all five types in characteristic >=5. Actual packaged code/output paths are verified separately.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete arithmetic classification for a distinguished singularity type of quartic del Pezzo resolutions. Five explicit realizable Frobenius classes are distinguished by rational chamber distributions; exact root-bearing refinements and 52 G-orbits measure rational big-linear-series behavior. Two individually indistinguishable negative-curve cycle partitions yield 17 versus 23 rational chambers, a motivated structural phenomenon not determined by the geometric count or simple splitting data. The classification is bounded by natural geometry rather than arbitrary size and is not a rename of the known 221-chamber theorem.
